edits.new:
**r8 (B1 riser and CR-end strain relief, CHG-R1-D03; H.23(s)).** On the r7 trunk the requirement rises from 1.216 mm above
the CR top at B1 to 7.555 mm, reached 2.675 mm past B1 (H.23(w)(1)). A level post at B1 and the r5 jacket bead cannot both
hold: W2 reaches B1 4.26 mm from its joint, so its 5.0 mm bead ends at (25.80, 65.24), 0.74 mm past B1, where the jacket must
stand 4.538 mm above the CR top (H.23(s)). The trunk therefore climbs a ramp from the CR copper. The **B1 riser (B1R)** is a
machined insulating wedge (G10/FR-4 laminate or PEEK, ASSUMPTION) bonded to the CR top with the 0.05 mm acrylic transfer tape
of the feet (A.7). B1R replaces the 3.0 x 3.0 mm B1 bead spot. Its footprint is x 23.55-26.05, y 62.54-67.10 (11.40 mm²; the
+x edge lies on the W2 pad exclusion x 26.05). Its ramp face rises at 65 degrees from the toe at y 62.54 to an apex 9.78 mm
above the CR top at y 67.10 (H.23(s)).

The leads leave the CR copper at the toe and lie on the ramp face. From the apex the trunk spans free for 10.4 mm along its
path, through T2 at a rise of 5.1 degrees, to B3. **B3** becomes an insulating post that holds the trunk jacket bottom
10.7 mm above the CR top (14.965 mm above the MB): the CR maximum of the requirement, 10.168 mm, plus a 0.50 mm design margin
(ASSUMPTION: sag, wedge and post height tolerance), rounded up to 0.1 mm. From B3 the trunk runs level to the tab Y +x edge
(x 37.56). The full profile meets the requirement plus the margin at every 0.05 mm from T1 to x 37.56. The minimum margin is
0.504 mm at T2 (25.80, 69.60), where 9.497 mm is required and 10.001 mm is built above the CR top (H.23(s)).

The 65 degree slope is chosen because it is the shallowest computed slope at which W1 and W2 still join the trunk on the CR
copper: the ramp height at T1 is 0.13 mm, below the 0.800 mm W1/W2 jacket radius. At 55 and 60 degrees the latest toe is
y 60.25 and 61.45, and W1/W2 would join a raised trunk; at 70 degrees the apex rises to 10.39 mm (H.23(s)). Lead stiffness
can only lift a lead above the ramp face, so a lead that does not follow the face still meets the 3-D rule. The T-A-06
item (8) dry fit confirms that the leads can be dressed onto the 65 degree face.

**Strain relief (r8 restatement of the r5 bead).** RTV bonds >= 5.0 mm of each lead jacket from its joint, on the CR copper
up to the toe and on along the ramp face. The wedge is bonded to the CR, so the bead keeps its CR-end function on the ramp.
